How to respond to a bad review, without making it worse.

To respond to a bad review, wait until you are calm, check the job records, then post a short public reply that thanks them, owns anything that was genuinely your fault, gives one fact and offers to sort it out offline. Write it for the next customer reading, not to win the argument. If the review breaks Google's rules, such as a person who was never your customer, report it as well as replying.

How should you respond to a bad review?

Here is the short version. Most good replies follow the same five steps:

  1. Wait a few hours. Never reply angry, from the van, at 10pm. A reply stays up as long as the review does.
  2. Check the facts. Find the job, the quote, the messages and the photos. Work out what really happened.
  3. Reply in public, briefly. Thank them, own what was genuinely your fault, state one calm fact if something is wrong, and say how you will put it right.
  4. Take it offline. Give a phone number or say you will call. The details belong in a private conversation.
  5. Report it if it breaks the rules. Fake reviews, people who were never customers and abusive reviews can be reported to Google. An honest bad review cannot, however unfair it feels.

The point of the reply is not to change the reviewer's mind. It is to show the next homeowner, who is comparing you with three other firms, that you are calm, fair and still around when something goes wrong. Google also notes that the person who wrote the review is notified when you reply, and that they can still change their review after reading it. A good reply sometimes turns a 1 star into a 4.

What should you check before you reply?

The reply you regret is usually the one you wrote too fast. Before you type a word, go through this:

  • Is this a real customer? Search your jobs, invoices and messages for the name, the street and the date. If you cannot find them, see the section on fake reviews below.
  • Is any of it true? Be honest with yourself. Late, messy, poor communication and a bill higher than the quote are the usual complaints. If part of it is fair, say so.
  • What does the paperwork say? The written quote, any agreed changes and the dates you were on site settle most "you overcharged me" reviews.
  • Can you fix it? A return visit, a small refund on the part that went wrong, or a proper explanation often solves it. Decide before you reply so you can offer something real.
  • Who replies? Pick one person in the business. Partners, office staff and the apprentice should not all be replying, and nobody should reply from a personal account.

If the customer is genuine and you can fix the problem, call them first. A phone call before the public reply is usually easier than a written back and forth, and you can then mention in the reply that you have already spoken.

Bad review reply templates you can copy

Change the details and keep them short. Three to five sentences is plenty. Use the customer's first name only, and never their address, job price or anything private.

1. The complaint is fair

"Thanks for telling us, [Name]. You are right that we left the site in a mess on the last day, and that is not good enough. I am sorry. I have called you to arrange a return visit to clear it properly this week, at no charge."

2. Partly fair, partly not

"Thanks for the feedback, [Name]. We are sorry the job ran two days over; the extra time came from the rotten joists we found and discussed with you on site, but we should have kept you better updated in writing. We have changed how we send updates as a result. If anything is still not right, please call me on [number]."

3. Unhappy with the price

"Thanks for your review, [Name]. Our price was the fixed figure in the written quote you accepted, and we did not add anything to it. I understand it is a big spend, and I am happy to go through what was included on a call. My number is [number]."

4. Angry, but no details

"Hi [Name], I am sorry to see this. I cannot find what went wrong from the review, and I would like to understand it and put it right. Please call me on [number] or message us through our website."

5. You cannot find them as a customer

"Hi [Name], we take every review seriously, but we cannot find any job, quote or call under this name or in this area. If we have missed something, please contact us on [number] so we can look into it."

6. A one star with no text at all

"Hi [Name], thanks for rating us. We would really like to know what we could have done better. If you are happy to tell us, please call [number]."

Template 5 matters. It tells future customers the review may not be real, without calling anyone a liar, which you cannot prove in public.

What should you never say in a reply?

A bad reply does more damage than the review. Avoid these:

  • Arguing point by point. Long replies read as defensive. Pick the one fact that matters.
  • Private details. Their address, what they paid, their payment history or anything about their home.
  • Insults or sarcasm, even if the review is rude.
  • Threats. No "remove this or you will hear from my solicitor". In the USA, the Federal Trade Commission's rule on consumer reviews, in force since October 2024, bans using unfounded legal threats, intimidation or false accusations to stop or remove a negative review.
  • Offers in exchange for removal. Google's review policies, updated in February 2026, say businesses must not offer incentives such as money, discounts or free work to get a review posted, changed or removed. The FTC also warns that paying people to remove truthful negative reviews may be unfair or deceptive.
  • Fake positive reviews to bury it. In the UK, the ban on fake reviews under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act came into force on 6 April 2025, and Google removes reviews it sees as fake engagement.

If you think a review is defamatory and it is costing you real work, speak to a lawyer in your country before you do anything. Do not hint at it in public.

This guide is general information, not legal or financial advice.

Can you get a bad Google review removed?

Only if it breaks Google's rules. Google is blunt about this: you can report any review, but only those that violate its policies are removed, and you should not report a review just because you disagree with it. Google says it does not get involved in disputes between businesses and customers.

The policies that most often apply to trade reviews are:

PolicyWhat it looks like for a trade business
Fake engagementA review from someone who never used you, or a sudden burst of 1 star reviews
Conflict of interestA competitor, an employee you let go, or a former business partner
Off topicA rant about something that has nothing to do with the job, such as politics or a neighbour dispute
Harassment or hate speechPersonal attacks on you or your staff
Personal informationYour home address, a worker's phone number or a car registration posted without consent
ImpersonationSomeone posting as another person or another business

To report a review:

  1. Go to your Business Profile and select Read reviews.
  2. Next to the review, select Report.
  3. Pick the reason that fits best and send the report.
  4. Check the status in Google's Reviews Management Tool. Google says evaluation typically takes several days.
  5. If it comes back as "no policy violation" and you still disagree, the same tool lets you submit a one time appeal.

Reply to the review anyway while you wait. If it is removed, your reply goes with it. If it stays, you have already shown customers your side calmly.

What if the reviewer was never your customer?

This is one of the most common questions on contractor forums, and it is frustrating. Do three things:

  • Check carefully first. People review under nicknames, a partner's name or a landlord's account. Search your records by street and date, not just the name.
  • Report it as fake engagement or conflict of interest, whichever fits. If the same account has left a pattern of odd reviews, you can also report the user profile in the Google Maps app.
  • Reply with template 5. Calm and factual. Never accuse a named competitor in public, even if you are sure.

If a real review you earned disappears, it may have been caught by Google's automated spam filter. Google says this sometimes removes legitimate reviews by mistake, and you can contact Business Profile support about it.

What if someone demands money to remove bad reviews?

Trade press including roofing and HVAC publications have reported scams where a business gets a sudden wave of 1 star reviews, then a message on WhatsApp, Telegram or email asking for money to make them stop. Google now has a dedicated form for this. Its advice is clear:

  • Do not reply to, negotiate with or pay them. Google says paying does not guarantee removal and can encourage more attempts.
  • Screenshot every message straight away, showing the date, time and the sender's number, email or profile.
  • Copy the links to each suspicious review.
  • Fill in Google's merchant extortion report form with all of it attached.

You can still post a short reply to the fake reviews, such as template 5, so customers see you are on it.

Can you ask a customer to change a bad review?

Yes, once you have genuinely fixed the problem, you can ask politely, once. You cannot make it a condition of the fix, and you cannot offer anything in return. Something like this works:

"Hi [Name], it is [your name] from [business]. I hope the new fence panels are holding up well. Thanks for giving us the chance to put it right. If you feel the review no longer reflects how things ended, you are welcome to update it, but no pressure either way."

Then leave it. If they update it, Google shows the new date on the review. If they do not, your public reply already tells the story of a business that came back and fixed it.

Will one bad review hurt your business?

Less than you think, if you have enough good ones. Here is the simple average to show why. Google's shown rating may not be a perfectly simple average, but it is close enough to make the point:

Before the bad reviewAfter one 1 star review
20 reviews averaging 4.8(20 x 4.8 + 1) / 21 = about 4.6
60 reviews averaging 4.8(60 x 4.8 + 1) / 61 = about 4.7
150 reviews averaging 4.8(150 x 4.8 + 1) / 151 = still about 4.8

So the real fix for bad reviews is lots of honest good ones. Ask every customer at the end of every job. Google's 2026 policy update also bans selectively asking only happy customers, so ask everyone and let the numbers work. Your website helps too. A page with real project photos, the towns you cover and how you handle problems gives a nervous customer a second place to check you out. If you want your profile set up and managed properly, see our Google Business Profile service.

Do this now

Your checklist.

  1. 01Wait a few hours and never reply angry
  2. 02Find the job, quote, messages and photos before writing
  3. 03Call genuine customers first if you can fix the problem
  4. 04Post a short public reply: thanks, own it, one fact, offer to talk
  5. 05Never share private details, threaten or offer anything for removal
  6. 06Report reviews that break Google's policies and track them in the Reviews Management Tool
  7. 07Screenshot and report any demand for money to Google's extortion form
  8. 08Ask every customer for a review after every job
Quick answers

Common questions.

Should you respond to bad reviews?

Yes. A calm, short reply shows future customers how you handle problems, and Google notifies the reviewer, who can then change their review. Silence looks like you do not care.

How do you respond to a negative review that is a lie?

Stay factual and do not call them a liar. Say what your records show in one sentence, offer to talk offline, and report the review to Google if it breaks a policy such as fake engagement.

Can I get a bad Google review removed?

Only if it breaks Google's content policies, for example spam, a conflict of interest, harassment or someone who was never a customer. Report it from your Business Profile; you get one appeal if the report is turned down.

How long does Google take to remove a reported review?

Google says review evaluation typically takes several days. You can check the status in its Reviews Management Tool, which shows whether a decision is pending, no violation was found or an appeal was escalated.

Can I offer a discount to remove a bad review?

No. Google's review policies ban offering money, discounts or free work in exchange for posting, changing or removing a review, and regulators such as the FTC warn against paying to remove truthful negative reviews.

How quickly should I reply to a bad review?

Within a day or two is a good aim, but only once you are calm and have checked the facts. A thoughtful reply the next morning beats an angry one in ten minutes.
